By Mike Allen · Aug 13, 2026

Happy Friday Jr.! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 579 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Amy Stern for copy editing.

🏗️ Breaking: The Kennedy Center board decided today to move forward with a two-year closure of the sprawling performing arts venue to allow for substantial renovation work. Some outdoor programming may continue.

  • The board voted to inscribe President Trump's name on the building beneath the main signage: "Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump." (N.Y. Times gift link)
 
 
1 big thing: Put it on his tab
 
Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: Suzanne Plunkett - Pool via Getty Images

The East Wing is gone, a new helipad is spreading across the South Lawn, and scaffolding wraps around the White House's front columns. But the price tag for President Trump's renovations is far less obvious, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

  • The muddled mix of funding streams includes private donors, taxpayers and, Trump has said, the president himself.

🤑 One tally finds that the president's construction projects — including his new East Wing ballroom, upgrades to Lafayette Square and more — could cost at least $927 million, The Washington Post reports (gift link).

  • Senate Democrats are urging the Government Accountability Office to audit the ballroom project's scope and cost.
  • The lawmakers cited a lack of transparency and "limited congressional oversight, meaningful public input, and adherence to established federal processes." (Read the letter.)

🏗️ White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in a statement that Trump "continues to implement long-overdue and necessary renovations," calling him the "Builder-in-Chief."

  • Ingle said the East Wing project is "inextricably tied" to security concerns, and pointed to an alleged plot to attack this summer's UFC fight on White House grounds.

Keep reading.
 
 
2. 🥇 Gold goes bananas
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep. Chart: Emily Peck/Axios

Gold prices rose to their highest level in more than two months yesterday, hitting $4,465 an ounce, Axios' Emily Peck reports.

  • The last time gold rose 13% or more in a month was September 1999 — more than a quarter-century ago.

🖼️ The big picture: Gold's ascent signals that investors are expecting less inflation.

  • When the Iran war started, they generally believed inflation would heat up, and interest rates would rise.

📈 Yes, but: Last month's Fed meeting reassured many investors that interest rates weren't about to rise — and gold started climbing.

  • Yesterday's relatively benign inflation report offered even more assurance.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Luigi Mangione appears at a pretrial hearing in Manhattan Criminal Court on Tuesday. Photo: David Dee Delgado/Pool via Getty Images
  1. ⚖️ Luigi Mangione is expected to plead guilty tomorrow to federal stalking charges tied to the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, The New York Times reports. Mangione is also facing trial on a murder charge in New York State. If he pleads guilty in federal court, his lawyers may argue that New York's double jeopardy laws prevent a murder trial tied to the same event. Gift link.
  2. ⚓️ The Pentagon is sending the aircraft carrier USS George Washington to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, The Wall Street Journal reports. The Abraham Lincoln has been at sea for a record 200 days, and lawmakers and others have raised concerns about conditions aboard the ship. Gift link.
  3. 📺 American Action Network, a top outside group aligned with House GOP leaders, is launching a $22 million ad campaign across 41 congressional districts. Scoop from Stef W. Kight.
  4. 💰 A Powerball ticket sold at a western Illinois gas station was the sole winner of last night's $1 billion jackpot. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 📸 Pic to go: Eclipse from space
 
Animation: CIRA/NOAA

A NOAA weather satellite had one of the best seats in (or above) the house for yesterday's total solar eclipse.

  • Above, you can see the Moon's shadow fall across the Earth from the Arctic Ocean down to Western Europe.
